observations: Photo 0 shows a black PS4 console with "PS4" visible on the front right bezel, two DUALSHOCK 4 controllers (one black, one custom painted teal/blue with red accents), a power cable, and a small taped paper between the controllers.
Photo 1 is a top-down view of the same console with the PlayStation logo on the top left, both controllers, and a power brick with cable.
Photo 2 shows the console from an angle with a UK 3-pin power plug; the console body has the original angular "Fat" design rather than the Slim or Pro.

claims.evidence: The console shape matches the original PS4 Fat in photos 0-2, but the 500GB storage capacity is not visible anywhere in the photos.
No screen, system menu, or power-on test is shown in any photo, so hack status and functionality cannot be confirmed remotely.
Photos show only the exterior; no boot test or gameplay demonstration is provided.

risks.risk: Console does not power on or has internal hardware failure.
risks.proof: Video of the PS4 booting to the home screen and navigating menus.
risks.if_unproven: as not working (parts or repair only)

risks.risk: One or both controllers do not connect, have stick drift, or dead batteries.
risks.proof: Video of both controllers syncing and responding to button inputs in system menus.

risks.risk: Storage is not 500GB or the system is modified/banned.
risks.proof: Screenshot of Settings > Storage showing 500GB and the system version.

risks.risk: Power supply is faulty or incompatible.
risks.proof: Video of the console powering on with the included cable and plug.
risks.if_unproven: as missing a working power supply

proof_requests: Video of the PS4 turning on, showing the home screen, and launching a game or app.
Video of both controllers pairing and responding to button inputs.
Photo or screenshot of system settings showing storage capacity (500GB) and model number.
Close-up photo of the model/serial sticker on the back of the console.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Sony PS4 console with two controllers and cables from the photos; because functionality and capacity cannot be verified remotely, it is priced at its worst case as non-working until proof is provided.
